goal: Distinguish remaining pure-proof, physical-read and reconstruction costs without selecting another blind repair.
procedure: Measure original seal/body/pair operations on a controlled native fixture with profiling/tracing absent; observe counts in a separate untimed invocation and verify no physical IO counters change. Read the existing observer source and primary Python profiling/current-frames documentation. Defer further proof tuning because local subcomponent timing does not establish cloud cost. Build an optional 50ms fixed-tag stack sampler using transient original-code ancestry and numeric aggregates only. Keep the actual fixture, targets, source hashes and permanent private-output suppression; no hooks, wrappers or deadline changes. Run RED missing-capability checks, then concurrency/privacy/bounds tests and unchanged original observer tests. Review before publication and dispatch one sample-mode diagnostic.
authority: Owner continuation authorizes exact result recovery and construction-method capture. Component checks and public procedure validation are distinct from live authority, response or learned-behavior qualification. No successful permission answer is retained or reused.
validation: Controlled original-code fixture: median per-call CPU origin seal 0.214ms, origin body 0.392ms, plain pair 0.960ms, inherited pair 1.184ms. Three runtime/fixture blobs match 4b88946f; IO counters unchanged. Nine missing-capability tests fail before implementation; nine new sampler and 32 existing observer checks then pass (41 cases/4.752s). Source runtime and aggregate observer remain unchanged. New real-engine sampling result remains pending; no measured overhead reduction or response improvement is claimed. Review then found a passing fixture could hide a failed sampler; an independent CLI regression failed on exit0 versus expected1. Separate fixture/observation statuses repair this. Final12 new+32 existing checks pass44 cases/4.183s; read-only correction review confirms no remaining findings.
failure_or_lesson: Python call-hook profiles add overhead to frequently called Python code, so tagged exclusive CPU must not become a predicted speedup. Sparse wall stack samples avoid call hooks but remain GIL/scheduling/native-call biased, can miss short jobs and retain approximate thread windows rather than exact lifecycle or CPU counts. Use them to discriminate the next design, not qualify latency. Keep sampler health separate from fixture success: observer errors or an observer still alive after close must not yield a passed diagnostic, while zero samples remain explicit unobserved coverage.
